verdict: Tested the M-L-M architecture's load-bearing assumption — that a learned latent predicts a held-out knockout's response — with a faithful Geneformer-style co-expression embedding + k-NN transfer, vs the 'predict the mean perturbation response' baseline. LATENT transfer reaches AUC 0.711 at predicting which genes move; the MEAN baseline reaches 0.693 — a gain of just 0.018. So the latent bridge helps only marginally over knowing NOTHING about which gene was hit, because most of a knockout's measured response is a GENERIC program (stress / proliferation / cell-cycle) shared across perturbations — which is exactly why 'predict the mean' is so hard to beat and why scGPT/Geneformer/GEARS have repeatedly failed to beat it in fair benchmarks (Ahlmann-Eltze 2024). Decisively for the proposal: the claimed MOAT is NOVEL mutations, and that is where transfer collapses — on the genes FARTHEST from any training twin the latent gain is -0.017 (AUC 0.653 vs mean 0.67); the model can only 'know the far-field effect' of a perturbation it has effectively already seen. So Phase 2 does NOT cross the transitivity wall — it relocates it into a latent space where the wall reappears as 'this perturbation is unlike anything in training.' A foundation model is worth wiring for INTERPOLATION (perturbations seen in other contexts — which our cross-cell-type result already does at r~0.6), not for the physics-guided NOVEL missense that is the pitch. Recommendation before building Phase 2: none of scGPT/Geneformer will beat this baseline on novel perturbations; if a learned model is used, it must be reported against the mean baseline and the novel-stratum, or it will look better than it is.
